summary: Intro kickoff between Redwood CS/SE and Cedarbrook infra + security. Customer intends to run conversational summarization and private search features behind their app with strict data residency and KMS requirements. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, VPC peering, SSO/SAML integration, and a 4-week activation runbook with checkpoints for staging, pilot, and go-live. Action items and owners captured.
topics: Security & compliance needs (KMS, encryption, audit logs)
Deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated capacity
transcript: 00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros. I am Maya, AE. Samir from our CSM team and Alex our SE will cover technicals. 00:12 Lena (Cedarbrook): Hi, Lena here. Head of ML, running the summarization pipeline. 00:18 Omar (Cedarbrook): Omar platform eng. We're responsible for infra and network. 00:22 Priya (Cedarbrook): Priya from security. We'll be leading the compliance review. 00:28 Maya: Great, thanks. The goal here is to align on onboarding runway — what we need for security sign-off, staging tests, and how we get you to pilot in production safely. 00:41 Alex (Redwood SE): Quick note — there are two main paths: our hosted API for fastest time-to-value, or Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and private networking. We'll talk through the tradeoffs. 00:55 Lena: Our priority is data isolation and auditability. We have PII in logs and we need KMS integration. We also want to keep latency under 400ms for summary queries at 512 tokens. 01:12 Maya: Understood. Priya, could you surface any non-negotiable controls? 01:18 Priya: SSO/SAML is mandatory, SOC2 attestation required, audit logs persisted 13 months, and keys must integrate with our HSM/KMS. Also need data residency in us-east-1. 01:32 Samir (Redwood CSM): That's common; we have a Private deployment option with customer-managed control plane and on-prem packaging for air-gapped needs. For KMS we support customer-managed keys — we'll include integration docs. 01:46 Omar: Networking — we want to avoid public endpoints. Is VPC peering or PrivateLink supported? 01:53 Alex: Yes, we support VPC peering and PrivateLink depending on cloud. For Dedicated we can put inference workers in your VPC or establish private endpoints. There are small differences in egress and routing for telemetry. 02:06 Priya: What about logs? We need redact options and export to our SIEM. 02:11 Alex: You can configure token-level logging and we have hooks to stream audit logs to customer S3 or to their Splunk/Datadog. We can apply redaction filters but we'll want to define those rules before pilot. 02:24 Lena: Good. On performance: we tested an open model internally and saw KV cache thrash. How do you handle prefix caching and batching? 02:33 Alex: The runtime supports automatic KV caching and workload-aware batching. For summarization with many short requests we recommend smaller batch windows to avoid latency spikes and enable prefix caching for repeated contexts. We'll run a tuning workshop to set batch sizes, max-latency SLO, and cache TTL. 02:50 Maya: Let's walk through the proposed 4-week activation runbook. Week 0 (this week) — intake and security checklist. Week 1 — staging environment and smoke tests. Week 2 — pilot with limited production traffic and performance tuning. Week 3 — go/no-go and cutover plan. 03:10 Omar: Sounds reasonable; do we need dedicated GPUs from the start? 03:15 Alex: For predictable p50/p95 latency at scale, Dedicated is recommended. Hosted can work for initial validation but might introduce variability. We can provide a short Dedicated proof-of-performance quote for your traffic shape. 03:30 Priya: Pricing aside, our compliance team will need the full SOC2 report and KMS encryption details. 03:36 Maya: We'll share the security pack after the call with SOC2, ISO docs, pen test summary, and the network checklist. 03:44 Lena: Also, we intend to measure QA success by 1) latency p95 < 900ms under pilot load, 2) summary accuracy above baseline on our eval set, and 3) zero PII leakage in logs. 03:59 Samir: We'll tie those into the runbook as explicit acceptance criteria. 04:05 Alex: For the pilot we'll ask for a representative traffic dump — ideally per-minute QPS distribution and a 500-record sample of inputs (sanitized). That helps us size kernels and recommend quantization or model variants. 04:20 Omar: On quantization — do you do INT8/is there quality regression risk? 04:25 Alex: We recommend specific quantization profiles per model. There's a small quality delta on some open models; we'll provide regression tests and a recommended fallback model for critical paths. 04:36 Lena: We also have to consider data residency; can we pin to us-east-1 and ensure logs don't leave region? 04:42 Maya: Yes, we can pin region for instances and ensure log storage is region-bound; details in the security pack. 04:50 Priya: Can you provide SAML metadata for SSO? 04:53 Maya: Yes, we'll provide the SAML SP metadata and a checklist. We'll also include steps for role mapping and SCIM. 05:03 Daniel (Product): Regarding rollout, we want canary percentage gating. Is A/B testing supported? 05:08 Alex: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary deploys and automatic fallback policies. You can route a percentage to a new model version and roll back automatically if regressions fire. 05:20 Samir: On operational visibility — you'll get per-route latency, token cost, and traces. We can set retention windows and alerting thresholds. 05:30 Lena: Excellent. Any blockers from our side? 05:34 Omar: We'll need the staging VPC IP ranges and any firewall rules we must open. Also an IAM role for S3 access if you stream logs. 05:44 Maya: We'll send a detailed network checklist with CIDR ranges and ports. 05:50 Alex: One more item — for initial tuning, please confirm expected max sequence length and median sequence length; that drives memory and batch config. 05:58 Lena: Median is about 120 tokens, max up to 2,048 for long-form docs. 06:05 Alex: Noted. That suggests we should tune kernels for mixed-length workloads and possibly use multi-stage batching. 06:12 Priya: What's the escalation path during pilot incidents? 06:16 Samir: We'll assign a dedicated CSM and SE, and Redwood provides 24/7 pager for Dedicated customers as an add-on. We'll capture on-call contacts in the runbook. 06:28 Maya: Recap — Redwood sends security pack, SSO metadata, network checklist, and Dedicated proof-of-performance quote. Cedarbrook provides sample traffic, PII classification, and confirms KMS/HSM constraints. We target the runbook workshop next Wednesday, Oct 6. 06:44 Lena: Agreed. 06:46 Omar: One last thing — can we run a short synthetic load test to validate p95 on Dedicated before pilot? 06:51 Alex: Yes, we'll provision a staging Dedicated cluster and run a 30-minute synthetic at projected QPS. Results will be in the benchmark sheet we share. 06:59 Priya: Good. Thanks all. 07:01 Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes and tasks. 07:04 [meeting ends]
